paragraphs.text: Junk food is now a staple of many Americans' diets. Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise. But recent studies show a lack of exercise is not to blame for rising obesity rates. Bad diets are.

sentences.text: But recent studies show a lack of exercise is not to blame for rising obesity rates.

sentences.text: Interventions(干预) to help reduce junk food consumption are especially important for children and teenagers.

analysis.translationLiteral: 旨在减少垃圾食品摄入的干预措施，对儿童和青少年尤其重要。
analysis.translationNatural: 要少碰垃圾食品，对孩子们——尤其是青少年——特别得上心。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Interventions(干预)】 (to help reduce junk food consumption) _are especially important_ (for children and teenagers).
analysis.structureSummary: 主语 + 不定式后置定语 + 系表 + for 状语

components.note: 主语，Interventions 指『干预措施』，括号中文『干预』是原文就带的中文注释，须照抄；to help reduce... 作后置定语

components.part: to help reduce junk food consumption
components.note: 不定式短语作后置定语，修饰 interventions，说明干预的目的是『减少垃圾食品摄入』
系表结构，are 系动词，especially important 作表语，强调『尤其重要』
for 引出对象，说明对『儿童和青少年』尤其重要

clauses: 本句是简单句，没有从句；主干为「主语 + 不定式后置定语 + 系表 + for 状语」。

phrases.meaning: 帮助（help sb do sth / help with）；帮助（不可数）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：help sb do/to do（不带 doing）/ can't help doing（忍不住）。常见搭配：help sb do sth / help with。

phrases.example: Data reduces the likelihood of errors. 数据能降低出错的可能性。

phrases.meaning: 食物（一般不可数）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：food（食物，泛指不可数）/ foods（多种食品，可数）。常见搭配：food supply / fast food。
phrases.example: Food prices are rising. 食品价格在上涨。

pitfalls: 注意区分：help sb do/to do（不带 doing）/ can't help doing（忍不住）。
注意区分：reduce（及物，减少某物）/ decrease（不及物，自身减少）/ lower（降低）。

sentences.text: Prevention is better than cure because obesity is so difficult to treat.

analysis.translationLiteral: 预防胜于治疗，因为肥胖极难医治。
analysis.translationNatural: 防患于未然好过亡羊补牢，毕竟肥胖一旦形成就极难治疗。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Prevention】 ~is better than cure~ {because obesity is so difficult to treat}.
analysis.structureSummary: 主系表 + because 原因状语从句

components.note: 主语，指『预防』，谓语用 is
表语，better than cure 意为『胜过治疗』，呼应谚语 Prevention is better than cure

components.part: because obesity is so difficult to treat
components.note: because 引导原因状语从句，说明为什么预防更重要——肥胖很难治
从句主语，肥胖

clauses: 状语从句「because obesity is so difficult to treat」：because 引导原因状语从句，说明为什么预防更重要——肥胖很难治
本句含比较结构（比较级 + than），than 后是被比较对象。
句中含从属连词引导状语从句，说明原因、目的、条件或时间。

phrases.meaning: 更好的；更好地（good/well 的比较级）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：better（更好）/ had better（最好，后接动词原形）。常见搭配：better than / a better understanding。
phrases.example: Sleep is better than more coffee. 睡眠比多喝咖啡更管用。

phrases.meaning: 困难的；难以……的
phrases.usage: 常见搭配：difficult to do / a difficult choice。
phrases.example: This word is difficult to pronounce. 这个词很难念。

pitfalls: 比较级 + than 引出比较对象；两者比较用比较级，三者以上用最高级。
because 引导从句，because of 后只能接名词；两者不能混用。
analysis.paragraphRole: 本段讲为何要干预：对青少年尤其重要，因为肥胖难治、预防胜于治疗，但健康教育虽对幼儿有效，却难触达青少年。

sentences.text: Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach.

analysis.translationLiteral: 不幸的是，尽管健康教育在幼童中已显出一些成效，青少年却更难被触达。
analysis.translationNatural: 可惜，健康教育虽说对小小孩有点用，到了青少年这儿却怎么都打不动。
analysis.structMarkup: (Unfortunately), {while health education has shown some success among young children}, 【teens】 _have been harder to reach_.
analysis.structureSummary: 评注状语 + while 让步状语从句 + 主句系表

components.note: 评注性状语，表达遗憾的语气，与上句『预防重要』形成落差

components.part: while health education has shown some success among young children
components.note: while 引导让步状语从句，意为『尽管』健康教育在幼儿中有些成效
主句主语，指青少年
系表结构，harder to reach 表语，意为『更难触达/影响到』，与上句幼儿成效形成对比

clauses: 状语从句「while health education has shown some success among young children」：while 引导让步状语从句，意为『尽管』健康教育在幼儿中有些成效
句中含让步/对比连词，引导状语从句；主句不再用 but 呼应。
have + 过去分词构成完成时态，强调对现在的影响或动作的先后。

phrases.meaning: 不幸地、遗憾的是、不巧（修饰全句）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：unfortunately（不幸地、遗憾的是，常置句首用逗号隔开，修饰整句）/ fortunately（幸运地，反义）/ unfortunate（不幸的）/ sadly（近义）。
phrases.example: Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach. 可惜，健康教育虽说对小小孩有点用，到了青少年这儿却怎么都打不动。

phrases.meaning: 健康；医疗、卫生
phrases.usage: 注意区分：health（名词）/ healthy（形容词）。常见搭配：mental health / public health。
phrases.example: Social ties affect health. 社会联系影响健康。

phrases.meaning: 教育、培养；教育学
phrases.usage: 注意区分：education（教育，不可数）/ educational（教育的，形容词）/ higher / further education（高等/继续教育）/ education 与 training（training 侧重技能培训）。
phrases.example: Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach. 可惜，健康教育虽说对小小孩有点用，到了青少年这儿却怎么都打不动。

pitfalls: although/though 引导让步从句时，主句不能再用 but（汉语习惯会说「虽然……但是」）。
现在完成时不能与明确的过去时间点（如 yesterday、in 2020）连用。

paragraphs.text: Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising. The researchers argued that previous interventions have probably been unsuccessful because of a major flaw: they focused on a future, healthier you and assumed that this would be enough motivation for teenagers. In contrast, the new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers' instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy, and the value they place on social justice.

sentences.text: Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising.

analysis.translationLiteral: 如今一项大规模研究尝试了一种创新方法来改变青少年对健康饮食的态度，结果颇有希望。
analysis.translationNatural: 最近一项大样本研究换了个新思路去扭转青少年对健康饮食的态度，结果挺让人看到希望。
analysis.structMarkup: (Now) 【a large-scale study】 _has tried an innovative approach_ (to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating), _and the results are promising_.
analysis.structureSummary: 状 + 主 + 谓宾 + 不定式后置定语 + and 并列句

components.note: 时间状语，引出新进展
主语，核心词 study，large-scale 定语『大规模的』
谓语，try an approach 意为『尝试一种方法』，innovative 作定语『创新的』

components.part: to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating
components.note: 不定式作后置定语修饰 approach，说明该方法旨在『改变青少年对健康饮食的态度』
and 引导并列句，results 主语，promising 表语『有希望的』

clauses: have + 过去分词构成完成时态，强调对现在的影响或动作的先后。
本句主干为「状 + 主 + 谓宾 + 不定式后置定语 + and 并列句」，先找限定动词再切分修饰成分。

phrases.meaning: 研究、调查；学习 / 研究、学习
phrases.usage: 注意区分：study（研究，可数）/ research（研究，不可数）。常见搭配：a study on sth / research study。
phrases.example: The study tracked 200 teenagers. 这项研究追踪了 200 名青少年。

phrases.meaning: 改变、变化 / 变化、零钱
phrases.usage: 注意区分：change（改变）/ exchange（交换）/ alter（改动，更正式）。常见搭配：change behaviour / climate change。
phrases.example: Attitudes are changing slowly. 态度正在缓慢改变。

phrases.meaning: 态度、看法、心态（attitude to/towards）（attitude 的复数/三单形式）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：attitudes（复数/三单）/ attitude（原形）。
phrases.example: Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising. 最近一项大样本研究换了个新思路去扭转青少年对健康饮食的态度，结果挺让人看到希望。

pitfalls: 现在完成时不能与明确的过去时间点（如 yesterday、in 2020）连用。

paragraphs.text: To do this, researchers had students read an article on the food industry. It revealed a secret about the manipulative and deceptive strategies used to make junk food more addictive and characterize the products as healthy. The article also explained how advertising campaigns specifically target very young and poor people, causing harm for these vulnerable groups. Afterwards, the participants read a fictional survey of teens who wanted to "fight back against the companies by buying and eating less processed food"

paragraphs.text: After the intervention, participants associated healthy eating with autonomy and social justice. The teenagers also rated healthy eating as being more appealing. Importantly, there were also some promising effects of the new intervention on actual behavior. A day later the students were offered a choice of snacks and drinks in a seemingly unrelated context. The teens chose healthy snacks and drinks (such as fruit or water) more often over unhealthy options (like biscuits and soda). Apparently associating a healthy diet with teenagers' own values seems to be a promising avenue to prevent obesity.

questions.stem: What do we learn about advertising campaigns from the snack food companies?

options.text: They convey the idea that their products are ok if consumers exercise more.
They send the message that bad diets are responsible for Americans' obesity.
They usually feature sports stars to emphasize the benefits of their snack foods.
They claim that lack of exercise is to blame for the increasing obesity rates.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about health education?

options.text: It has shed light on teens' instinct for rebellion and autonomy.
It has placed much more emphasis on cure than on prevention.
It has contributed little to the campaigns against obesity.
It has largely failed to turn teens away from junk food.

questions.stem: What is a major flaw in previous interventions to help reduce junk food consumption?

options.text: They motivated teens to stay away from junk food only temporarily.
They focused on the benefits young people would reap in the future.
They were based on the assumption that motivation was the only key.
They were incapable of appealing to teens' instinct for rebelliousness.

questions.stem: In what way is the new intervention innovative?

options.text: It emphasizes people's sense of social responsibility.
It cleverly exploits teenagers' personal weaknesses.
It takes advantage of teenagers' natural inclination.
It promises immediate rather than future benefits.

questions.stem: What conclusion can be drawn from the new research?

options.text: A totally different approach could be adopted to combat advertising campaigns for snack food.
An effective intervention has to be found to persuade teenagers to switch to a healthier lifestyle.
Obesity can be hopefully prevented by building links between teenagers' values and healthy eating.
An innovative way to beat obesity is to expose food companies' manipulative and deceptive practices.

examples: The researchers argued that previous interventions have probably been unsuccessful because of a major flaw: they focused on a future, healthier you and assumed that this would be enough motivation for teenagers. 研究者觉得，老法子之所以多半不灵，毛病出在一个关键处：它们只拿『将来更健康的你』说事，以为这就够让青少年心动了。
Texting probably isn't destroying their ability. 发短信大概不会毁掉他们的能力。

more.confusables: probably（很可能）/ perhaps（也许）/ possibly（或许，可能性更低）

processed.sense: 过程、流程（process 的过去式/过去分词形式）
examples: Afterwards, the participants read a fictional survey of teens who wanted to "fight back against the companies by buying and eating less processed food" 接着，参与者还读到一份虚构的青少年问卷——那些孩子想『靠少买少碰加工食品来跟这些公司对着干』。

more.confusables: processed（过去式/过去分词）/ process（原形）

examples: Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise. 零食品牌的广告常请体育明星站台，放出话来：只要多运动，吃我家零食的坏处就能一笔勾销。

more.confusables: products / productivity / production（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

rated.sense: 评价、评级、评估、列为（rate 的过去式）；有…评级的
examples: The teenagers also rated healthy eating as being more appealing. 青少年还觉得，健康饮食变得更对胃口了。

more.confusables: rated / rate（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

rates.sense: 比率、率、费率、价格、速度（复数）；评价、评级（第三人称单数）
examples: But recent studies show a lack of exercise is not to blame for rising obesity rates. 但新近的研究却说：发胖不能怪运动少。

more.confusables: rates / rate（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

reach.sense: 到达、抵达、达到；伸手够到、联系上；范围、可及之处

more.confusables: reach（到达；够到；达成，及物动词，直接接宾语，不加 to/at）/ arrive at/in（不及物，须带介词）/ reach an agreement（达成协议）/ get to（口语）/ out of reach（够不着）/ achieve（达成目标）

examples: Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach. 可惜，健康教育虽说对小小孩有点用，到了青少年这儿却怎么都打不动。

read.sense: 读、阅读；读懂、写着（过去式/过去分词同形，读 /red/；本文 most end users don't read EULAs 多数用户不读协议）
examples: To do this, researchers had students read an article on the food industry. 具体操作是：先让学生读一篇讲食品行业的文章。

more.confusables: read / reader / reading（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

examples: One recent study found a surprising result. 最近一项研究发现了意外的结果。

more.confusables: recent（最近的）/ recently（副词）/ resent（怨恨）

reduce.sense: 减少、降低（及物）；使沦为（reduce to）
examples: Data reduces the likelihood of errors. 数据能降低出错的可能性。

more.confusables: reduce（及物，减少某物）/ decrease（不及物，自身减少）/ lower（降低）

examples: The researchers argued that previous interventions have probably been unsuccessful because of a major flaw: they focused on a future, healthier you and assumed that this would be enough motivation for teenagers. 研究者觉得，老法子之所以多半不灵，毛病出在一个关键处：它们只拿『将来更健康的你』说事，以为这就够让青少年心动了。

more.confusables: researchers / researcher（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

examples: The results suggest a clear difference. 结果表明有明显差异。

more.confusables: results（复数）/ result（单数）

revealed.sense: 揭示、透露、揭露、显示、展现出（阅读中常指研究/调查显示）（reveal 的过去式/过去分词形式）
examples: It revealed a secret about the manipulative and deceptive strategies used to make junk food more addictive and characterize the products as healthy. 文章揭开了一个内幕：食品行业用种种套路把垃圾食品做得更让人上瘾，还硬把产品包装成健康货。

more.confusables: revealed（过去式/过去分词）/ reveal（原形）

rising.sense: 上升、增长、上涨、兴起；升起、起身、站起来（rise 的现在分词/动名词形式）
examples: But recent studies show a lack of exercise is not to blame for rising obesity rates. 但新近的研究却说：发胖不能怪运动少。

more.confusables: rising（现在分词/动名词）/ rise（原形）

seemingly.sense: 看似、表面上、似乎、看上去
examples: A day later the students were offered a choice of snacks and drinks in a seemingly unrelated context. 隔了一天，学生在一个看似不相干的场合被问要吃什么喝什么。

seems.sense: 似乎、好像（seem + adj. / seem to do）（seem 的复数/三单形式）
examples: Apparently associating a healthy diet with teenagers' own values seems to be a promising avenue to prevent obesity. 看来，把健康饮食和青少年自己的价值观绑在一起，倒真有可能是防肥胖的一条好路子。

more.confusables: seems（复数/三单）/ seem（原形）

show.sense: 显示、表明（show that）；展示 / 演出、展览
examples: The study shows how roles endure. 研究显示角色如何延续。

more.confusables: show（显示）/ prove（证明，更强）/ indicate（表明，正式）

shown.sense: 显示、表明、展示、给…看（show 的过去分词）
examples: Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach. 可惜，健康教育虽说对小小孩有点用，到了青少年这儿却怎么都打不动。

more.confusables: shown / show（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

examples: Simply feeling something is right is subjective. 仅仅感觉某事对，是主观的。

more.confusables: simply（仅仅/简单地）/ simple（简单的）/ simplistic（过于简化的）

snack.sense: 小吃、零食、点心；吃零食（snack foods / between-meal snacks）
examples: Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise. 零食品牌的广告常请体育明星站台，放出话来：只要多运动，吃我家零食的坏处就能一笔勾销。

more.confusables: snack / snacks（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

snacks.sense: 小吃、零食、点心；吃零食（snack foods / between-meal snacks）（snack 的复数/三单形式）
examples: A day later the students were offered a choice of snacks and drinks in a seemingly unrelated context. 隔了一天，学生在一个看似不相干的场合被问要吃什么喝什么。

more.confusables: snacks（复数/三单）/ snack（原形）

social.sense: 社会的、社会性的；社交的、交际的
examples: In contrast, the new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers' instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy, and the value they place on social justice. 而这新法子聪明的地方，就在于拿青少年的叛逆劲儿、自主意识，还有他们对『社会正义』的那份在意来借力。

more.confusables: social / society / socializing（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

soda.sense: 苏打水、汽水、苏打、碳酸饮料（soda water 苏打水；阅读中多见于含糖饮料话题）
examples: The teens chose healthy snacks and drinks (such as fruit or water) more often over unhealthy options (like biscuits and soda). 比起不健康的（比如饼干、汽水），这些孩子更常挑健康的零食和饮品（比如水果、白水）。

sports.sense: 体育运动（sport 的复数）；运动的（作定语）
examples: Sports coverage rarely mentions this. 体育报道很少提到这一点。

more.confusables: sports（运动，作定语）/ sport（一项运动）

stars.sense: 星、恒星；明星、主角、星形；主演、标星号（star in 主演；影视/天文话题）（star 的复数/三单形式）
examples: Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise. 零食品牌的广告常请体育明星站台，放出话来：只要多运动，吃我家零食的坏处就能一笔勾销。

more.confusables: stars（复数/三单）/ star（原形）

examples: They develop coping strategies. 他们发展出应对策略。

more.confusables: strategies（策略）/ strategy（单数）/ tactic（战术）

students.sense: 学生、大学生、学员（student 的复数）

more.confusables: student（学生，尤中学及以上/大学；也泛指研究者）/ pupil（尤英式，中小学生；也指瞳孔）/ study（学习；研究）/ studious（用功的）

examples: To do this, researchers had students read an article on the food industry. 具体操作是：先让学生读一篇讲食品行业的文章。

studies.sense: 研究（study 的复数）；study 的第三人称单数
examples: Studies suggest a strong link. 研究表明存在强关联。

more.confusables: studies（复数/三单）/ study（单数）

study.sense: 研究、调查；学习 / 研究、学习
examples: The study tracked 200 teenagers. 这项研究追踪了 200 名青少年。

more.confusables: study（研究，可数）/ research（研究，不可数）

examples: Hard work is not the only route to success. 努力并非成功的唯一路径。

more.confusables: success / successful（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

survey.sense: 调查（可数）/ 调查、审视
examples: A survey of 290 employees found a gap. 一项针对 290 名员工的调查发现了差距。

more.confusables: survey（调查）/ poll（民意调查）/ inspect（检查）

examples: The article also explained how advertising campaigns specifically target very young and poor people, causing harm for these vulnerable groups. 文章还点明，广告是如何精准锁定那些年幼和贫困的人，反过来坑了这群最弱势的人。

more.confusables: target / targets（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

teenagers.sense: 青少年、十几岁的年轻人（teenager 的复数，13–19 岁）
examples: Interventions(干预) to help reduce junk food consumption are especially important for children and teenagers. 要少碰垃圾食品，对孩子们——尤其是青少年——特别得上心。

teens.sense: 青少年（常用复数teens：十几岁；adj. 青少年的）（teen 的复数/三单形式）
examples: Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach. 可惜，健康教育虽说对小小孩有点用，到了青少年这儿却怎么都打不动。

more.confusables: teens（复数/三单）/ teen（原形）

examples: Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising. 最近一项大样本研究换了个新思路去扭转青少年对健康饮食的态度，结果挺让人看到希望。

more.confusables: towards / toward（同族不同词形，注意词性与用法）

treat.sense: 对待、看待、处理、治疗、款待、请客；款待、乐事（treat A as B 视 A 为 B；treatment 治疗）
examples: Prevention is better than cure because obesity is so difficult to treat. 防患于未然好过亡羊补牢，毕竟肥胖一旦形成就极难治疗。

tried.sense: 尝试、试图、努力、试用、试验、审理（try 的过去式/过去分词）
examples: Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising. 最近一项大样本研究换了个新思路去扭转青少年对健康饮食的态度，结果挺让人看到希望。

unfortunately.sense: 不幸地、遗憾的是、不巧（修饰全句）

more.confusables: unfortunately（不幸地、遗憾的是，常置句首用逗号隔开，修饰整句）/ fortunately（幸运地，反义）/ unfortunate（不幸的）/ sadly（近义）

examples: Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach. 可惜，健康教育虽说对小小孩有点用，到了青少年这儿却怎么都打不动。

used.sense: use 的过去式/过去分词；（be used to）习惯于；（used to）过去常常
examples: They used flexible work arrangements. 他们使用了弹性工作安排。

more.confusables: used to do（过去常常）/ be used to doing（习惯于）/ be used to do（被用来做）

value.sense: 价值、价格、重要性；价值观（values）；重视、珍视、估价

more.confusables: value（价值，不可数；values 价值观，复数；重视，动词）/ be of value = valuable / worth（只作表语，be worth doing）/ price（是「定价」，value 是「价值」）/ evaluate（评估，动词）

examples: In contrast, the new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers' instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy, and the value they place on social justice. 而这新法子聪明的地方，就在于拿青少年的叛逆劲儿、自主意识，还有他们对『社会正义』的那份在意来借力。

values.sense: 价值、价格、重要性；价值观（values）；重视、珍视、估价（value 的复数/三单形式）
examples: Apparently associating a healthy diet with teenagers' own values seems to be a promising avenue to prevent obesity. 看来，把健康饮食和青少年自己的价值观绑在一起，倒真有可能是防肥胖的一条好路子。

more.confusables: values（复数/三单）/ value（原形）

vulnerable.sense: 脆弱的、易受伤害的（be vulnerable to）
examples: Small farms are most vulnerable. 小农场最脆弱。

more.confusables: vulnerable to（易受……伤害）/ vulnerability（脆弱性）

wanted.sense: 想要（want to do / want sb to do）；需要（want 的过去式/过去分词形式）
examples: Afterwards, the participants read a fictional survey of teens who wanted to "fight back against the companies by buying and eating less processed food" 接着，参与者还读到一份虚构的青少年问卷——那些孩子想『靠少买少碰加工食品来跟这些公司对着干』。

more.confusables: wanted（过去式/过去分词）/ want（原形）

examples: Irrigation needs water. 灌溉需要水。

more.confusables: water（水，不可数）/ waters（水域）/ a water（一杯水）

young.sense: 年轻的、幼小的；青年的（本文指年轻人 / 年轻时）
examples: Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach. 可惜，健康教育虽说对小小孩有点用，到了青少年这儿却怎么都打不动。
